thread.title: If You Are Selling Apple Stock Today, Apple Will Probably Be Buying Them

author: Karl Kaufman
title: If You Are Selling Apple Stock Today, Apple Will Probably Be Buying Them
text:
Today's headlines about Apple's earnings will inevitably focus on the negatives. The company gave somewhat weaker holiday guidance and most notably, announced it will no longer break out iPhone sales in its quarterly reports. Who's howling the loudest over the change in iPhone reporting? Analysts, of course. As I wrote six months ago, analysts are almost always wrong when it comes to Apple estimates. Without the iPhone metric, their estimates will be further compromised.
Analysts and talking heads on CNBC have been criticizing Apple over the past few years for being too reliant on iPhone sales. Now that they are transitioning to the higher-margin services business, the complaints have shifted to a lack of transparency and that there's fear that Apple has something to hide.
I get it — Wall Street does not like uncertainty and goes crazy when confronted with unexpected change. But is the company worth 6-7% less than it was yesterday?
There was plenty to like in Apple's Q4 report. Earnings were $2.91 per share while revenue came in at $62.9 billion last quarter, which beat analyst's expectations of $2.79 earnings per share and $61.41 billion in revenue. Average Selling Prices (ASPs) for iPhones was $793, blowing away analyst's expectations of $750.93
The company said there was no sign of a growth slowdown in China, and recent positive news in U.S.-China trade talks should only help that.
Since Steve Jobs died in October 2011, Tim Cook has transformed Apple into a more shareholder-friendly company. Jobs disdained dividends, while under Cook's leadership, Apple paid its first dividend in many years in 2012 and has raised it consistently. Does Apple become a trillion dollar company with Jobs at the helm? I doubt it.
“Our install base is growing at double digits and that’s probably a much more significant metric for us from an ecosystem point of view and customer loyalty,” Cook said during Apple's conference call. “This is a little bit like if you go to the market and push the cart up to the cashier and she says, 'How many units do you have in there?' It doesn’t matter a lot how many units there are in there in terms of the overall value of what’s in the cart.”
The market will come to its senses, as there is solid reasoning behind not reporting iPhone sales. Apple is clearly repositioning itself and its overall strategy. The company announced it would be breaking out Services as a metric in their upcoming quarterly reports and will rename its vaguely titled "Other Services" section as "Wearables, Homes and Accessories."
With $237.1 billion in cash, the company is in the midst of a record-breaking $100 billion share buyback program, which it announced in May. Since the stock is trading down more than 6.5% as of this writing, I'm willing to bet the farm that Apple will be using a lot of that cash today to pick up more shares on sale.
Disclosure: The author and American Dream Investing own shares in AAPL.
